# Change-of-Control Extraction Report

## Executive Summary

This report reviews 8 acquisition-target contracts for change-of-control provisions. Each contract is analyzed below in a dedicated section that surfaces the change-of-control / anti-assignment definition, consent and termination triggers, financial exposures, reverse-triangular-merger analysis, and risk rating. The structured data behind these analyses (a 28-column extraction) is appended as a reference table.

## Per-Contract Findings

### hendricks-license-agreement

This section addresses the License Agreement between the Licensee (the acquisition target) and Hendricks Automation Systems, Inc. as Licensor, governed by Massachusetts law.

The contract contains a broadly drafted Change of Control definition in Section 1.3, which provides that "'Change of Control' means, with respect to Licensee, (a) any merger, consolidation, or reorganization involving Licensee, whether or not Licensee is the surviving entity; (b) the sale, transfer, or other disposition of all or substantially all of Licensee's assets; (c) the acquisition by any person or group of persons of beneficial ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding voting securities of Licensee; or (d) any other transaction or series of related transactions that results in a change in the identity of the person or persons who ultimately control Licensee" and further specifies that "a Change of Control shall be deemed to have occurred regardless of the form of transaction, including without limitation forward mergers, reverse mergers, triangular mergers, and any combination thereof." This language expressly forecloses any reverse-triangular structural workaround. No separate indirect Change of Control hook is provided beyond the Section 1.3 definition itself.

The anti-assignment clause at Section 10.1 compounds this exposure. It states that "Licensee shall not assign, transfer, delegate, or otherwise dispose of this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of Licensor, which consent may be withheld in Licensor's sole and absolute discretion" and further provides that "a Change of Control of Licensee shall be deemed an assignment by operation of law." Any violation renders the purported assignment "null and void and of no force or effect." The consent standard is therefore absolute discretion — the most adverse consent standard available.

Section 9.1 grants Hendricks an immediate termination right upon a Change of Control, with zero days' notice and zero cure period. No termination fee or buyout formula was extracted. The licensed technology — the FlowLogic Algorithm — is embedded as a core component of the AX-7000 Product Line (Exhibit A), and its loss would render that product line non-functional. Revenue exposure attributable to this agreement is $52,000,000. Revenue concentration percentage was not extracted. No equity acceleration findings were extracted.

The dependent systems implicated include the FlowLogic Algorithm, the AX-7000 Product Line, and the Crestline ERP Platform v.8.2; cross-referenced exhibits are Exhibit A (Description of Licensed Technology) and Exhibit B (Royalty Calculation Methodology).

Risk Rating: CRITICAL. The Section 1.3 definition eliminates all structural workarounds; Section 9.1 provides an immediate, no-notice, no-cure termination right; Section 10.1 requires consent withholdable at absolute discretion; and loss of the license constitutes a potential deal-killer given the $52,000,000 revenue exposure tied to the AX-7000 Product Line.

Action Items: (1) Engage Hendricks immediately to obtain prior written consent under Section 10.1 before signing or closing. (2) Negotiate a waiver or amendment of Section 9.1's immediate termination right or obtain a standstill covenant from Hendricks. (3) Negotiate an amendment to Section 1.3 carving out the specific acquisition structure. (4) Quantify the full AX-7000 revenue exposure as a critical deal-risk metric. (5) Conduct independent diligence on the Crestline ERP Platform v.8.2 license for its own change-of-control provisions. (6) Memorialize any consent in a written amendment or letter signed by an authorized Hendricks representative per Section 12.2. (7) Evaluate the Section 9.5(c) 90-day sell-off period as partial mitigation for AX-7000 inventory. (8) Assess alternative licensing or technology substitutes for FlowLogic as a contingency.

### hesse-employment-agreement

This section addresses the employment agreement (hesse-employment-agreement) between Apex Industrial Technologies, Inc. and Dr. Miriam Hesse, governed by Ohio law.

The agreement contains a standalone Change of Control definition at Section 1, which provides, in relevant part, that "Change of Control" means, among other events, any merger or consolidation "in which the holders of the Company's outstanding voting securities immediately prior to such transaction hold less than fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding voting securities of the surviving or resulting entity immediately following such transaction," or "the acquisition by any person or group … of beneficial ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the combined voting power of the Company's then-outstanding voting securities." No separate Change of Control definition covering indirect transfers is provided (coc_includes_indirect is false). The proposed reverse-triangular merger—in which Merger Sub merges into the Company with the Company surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Voltan Manufacturing Group, Inc.—independently satisfies the Section 1 ownership-threshold trigger, as existing Company stockholders will hold zero percent of the surviving entity post-closing. The Side Letter (Exhibit A) expressly confirms this conclusion.

The anti-assignment provision at Section 8.3 states that "Executive may not assign, delegate, or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of her rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the Company," while permitting Company assignment to a successor "provided that any such successor expressly assumes and agrees to perform the Company's obligations under this Agreement." The Section 8.3 consent standard is unspecified. Notably, Section 8.3 does not include operation-of-law language, but this is immaterial given that the Change of Control definition in Section 1 is independently triggered by the merger structure.

Triggering a Change of Control activates single-trigger automatic equity acceleration under Section 5.4, immediately vesting equity awards valued at $967,230. No termination of employment is required for this acceleration. In addition, a double-trigger cash severance obligation of $1,232,000 arises under Section 5.3(a) if Executive is terminated within 24 months post-closing. These figures do not yet account for any Section 280G / Section 5.5 parachute payment reduction analysis. No termination section, notice period, cure period, termination fee, or buyout formula cells were extracted. No revenue exposure or revenue concentration figures were extracted.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL. The single-trigger automatic equity acceleration of $967,230 vests upon consummation of the Merger without requiring Executive's termination, and the unresolved conflict between Section 5.4 and the Merger Agreement's Section 3.05 RSU Rollover Treatment constitutes a closing condition under Merger Agreement Section 7.03(c).

Action Items: (1) Resolve the conflict between Section 5.4 and Merger Agreement Section 3.05 prior to the expected August 29, 2025 Closing Date, as required by Side Letter Section 3. (2) Obtain Executive's written consent to RSU Rollover Treatment or a signed waiver of Section 5.4 acceleration rights at least five business days before closing, as required by Merger Agreement Section 7.03(c). (3) Ensure Parent executes a written assumption of the Employment Agreement at closing per Section 8.3. (4) Quantify and reserve for the $1,232,000 double-trigger severance and complete a Section 280G / Section 5.5 analysis for the combined obligations. (5) Confirm that the 15-business-day advance notice obligation under Section 5.1 has been or will be satisfied before the Closing Date. (6) Evaluate retention risk for the CTO role given the 24-month double-trigger severance window.

### apex-kenji-jv-agreement

This section addresses the Joint Venture Agreement (contract ID: apex-kenji-jv-agreement) between Apex and Kenji Valve Co., Ltd., governed by Delaware law.

The contract contains an explicit Change of Control definition in Article I, which provides that "'Change of Control' means, with respect to any Member, the acquisition, directly or indirectly, by any Person or group of Persons acting in concert (other than such Member's existing Affiliates as of the Effective Date), of fifty percent (50%) or more of the issued and outstanding voting equity interests of such Member, whether by purchase, merger, consolidation, recapitalization, reorganization, or otherwise, or any transaction or series of related transactions that results in a change in the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of such Member." This definition expressly captures indirect acquisitions and merger structures, including a reverse-triangular merger in which Apex survives as a wholly-owned subsidiary, because the acquirer would obtain indirect control of 100% of Apex's voting equity, plainly satisfying both the "directly or indirectly" and "50% or more" thresholds.

The anti-assignment provision is set forth in Section 11.1, which states: "No Member shall Transfer all or any portion of its Membership Interest without the prior written consent of the other Member, which consent may be withheld in such Member's sole and absolute discretion, except as expressly provided in Sections 11.2 and 11.3 of this Agreement." The anti-assignment clause includes transfers by operation of law. However, the Change of Control carve-out in Section 12.2 means that a qualifying Change of Control is not independently treated as a Transfer requiring consent under Section 11.1; instead, the operative mechanism is Kenji's Buy-Out Option under Section 12.3(a). No separate consent trigger or termination right is extracted — the contract does not provide Kenji a right to terminate upon a Change of Control, and no termination notice period, cure period, or termination fee is provided.

The financial exposure is significant. Apex's revenue contribution to the JV is $14,800,000 (representing 7.9% revenue concentration). If the Change of Control triggers Kenji's Buy-Out Option and the Section 12.3(b) Successor Entity carve-out does not apply, the Buy-Out Price formula — "four and one-half times (4.5x) the Company's trailing twelve-month EBITDA as of the last day of the Company's most recently completed Fiscal Year" — yields approximately $22.95M based on FY2024 EBITDA of $5.1M, payable in cash at closing. No equity acceleration value is extracted.

The risk rating is HIGH. The Change of Control definition in Article I unambiguously triggers on a reverse-triangular merger, activating Kenji's Buy-Out Option under Section 12.3(a) and creating a forced cash outflow of approximately $22.95M unless the Section 12.3(b) Successor Entity carve-out applies — which requires the acquirer's consolidated annual fluid control revenue to exceed $500,000,000 and satisfaction of management retention commitments.

Action items: (1) Determine prior to closing whether the acquirer's fluid control revenue exceeds $500M to assess applicability of the Section 12.3(b) carve-out. (2) If the carve-out does not apply, prepare for or negotiate around the ~$22.95M cash Buy-Out obligation. (3) If pursuing the carve-out, ensure written management retention commitment is delivered within 30 days post-closing under Section 12.3(b)(i). (4) Deliver Change of Control notice to Kenji within 10 business days of signing the definitive merger agreement and again within 5 business days of consummation under Section 12.1. (5) Ensure the Successor Entity executes a joinder agreement within 30 days post-closing under Section 12.4(b). (6) Separately review the Technology License Agreement and Distribution Access Agreement, both cross-referenced herein, for independent change-of-control or assignment triggers.

### credit-agreement-summit

This section addresses the Credit Agreement with Summit National Bank, N.A. (contract_id: credit-agreement-summit), classified as a credit agreement governed by Ohio law.

The agreement contains dual, overlapping change-of-control triggers. First, Section 1.01 defines "Change of Control" to include, among other events, acquisition by any person or group of "more than 50% of the outstanding shares of Voting Stock of the Borrower" or the Borrower ceasing to own "100% of the Equity Interests of each of its Subsidiaries (other than Apex-Kenji Precision JV, LLC, in which the Borrower shall at all times maintain an ownership interest of not less than 51%)." This definition expressly covers indirect ownership changes (coc_includes_indirect: True), meaning it triggers in a reverse-triangular merger upon closing. Second, Section 8.01(j) establishes a separate, lower-threshold "Change in Control" Event of Default at 35% beneficial ownership — a threshold that is equally and independently satisfied by the proposed transaction.

The anti-assignment provision at Section 10.05 states: "The Borrower may not assign or otherwise transfer any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of all Lenders." Critically, this consent standard is absolute discretion — no reasonableness qualifier applies — and the clause does not include "by operation of law or otherwise" language (anti_assignment_includes_operation_of_law: False). As the reverse-triangular merger analysis confirms, however, the omission of operation-of-law language is immaterial given the explicit dual CoC/CiC definitions that trigger independently.

The financial exposure is $75,000,000 in revolving commitments. Triggering Section 2.09(d) would require mandatory prepayment within 30 days with no cure period. No termination fee amount or buyout formula is extracted. No equity acceleration value is provided. Revenue concentration percentage is not extracted.

The risk rating is CRITICAL. This rating is authoritative: the agreement imposes dual change-of-control triggers (>50% under Section 1.01; >35% under Section 8.01(j)), mandatory prepayment of up to $75,000,000 within 30 days, automatic acceleration upon Event of Default under Section 8.02(a), and unanimous lender consent with no reasonableness standard under Section 10.05 — collectively representing deal-killer exposure.

Action items: (1) Obtain unanimous written lender consent under Section 10.05 prior to closing. (2) Negotiate waiver or amendment of the Section 2.09(d) mandatory prepayment obligation. (3) Negotiate waiver or amendment of the Section 8.01(j) Change in Control Event of Default. (4) Confirm any definitional amendments require unanimous consent per Section 10.02(e). (5) Arrange replacement financing if waivers cannot be obtained. (6) Deliver notice to Administrative Agent within 5 Business Days per Sections 2.09(d) and 5.07(c). (7) Review cross-default implications against Schedule 3.08 Material Contracts. (8) Confirm post-closing Apex-Kenji JV ownership satisfies the 51% covenant under Section 1.01(b).

### northland-refining-msa

This section addresses the Northland Refining Corporation Supply Agreement (Contract No. MSA-2019-0042), a supply agreement governed by Ohio law.

No separate change-of-control definition is provided in this contract. The sole relevant restriction is the anti-assignment provision at Section 14.2, which states: "Neither Party shall assign, transfer, or delegate this Agreement or any of its rights, interests, or obligations hereunder, in whole or in part, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent may be withheld in such Party's sole and absolute discretion. Any purported assignment, transfer, or delegation in violation of this Section 14.2 shall be null and void and of no force or effect." Section 14.2 further provides that affiliate assignments are permitted without consent, subject to thirty-day notice and joint-and-several liability of the assigning party — a carve-out that does not assist the Acquirer, which is not a pre-existing affiliate of Apex.

The phrase "whether by operation of law or otherwise" is dispositive for merger-structure analysis. Under UCC § 2-210 as applied in Ohio — the governing law for this goods supply agreement covering precision fluid control valves, actuators, and integrated assemblies (AX-3000 through AX-7000 series) — this language is likely to trigger the consent requirement even in a reverse-triangular merger where Apex survives as a wholly-owned subsidiary. The consent standard is Northland's "sole and absolute discretion," carrying no reasonableness obligation. Accordingly, Northland could withhold consent with no legal exposure, creating a potential deal-stopper. No termination section, termination notice period, cure period, termination fee, or buyout formula was extracted, meaning that if a violation occurs, the contract is simply null and void under Section 14.2 with no structured exit mechanism.

The financial exposure is $30,000,000 in annual revenue, tied to the Section 2.3 Minimum Purchase Commitment, which exceeds the $25M critical threshold.

This contract is rated CRITICAL. The combination of absolute-discretion consent withholding, "operation of law" trigger language applicable under Ohio UCC § 2-210, and $30M+ annual revenue exposure makes this a potential transaction-blocking risk requiring immediate pre-closing action.

Action items: (1) Engage Northland immediately to seek written consent under Section 14.2 before closing. (2) Confirm Ohio UCC § 2-210 analysis with local counsel regarding the reverse-triangular merger structure. (3) Evaluate whether recasting the merger structure can avoid the "operation of law" trigger. (4) Negotiate replacement of "sole and absolute discretion" with a "not to be unreasonably withheld" standard. (5) Validate the $30–$38M annual revenue exposure in deal valuation and risk disclosures. (6) Review Exhibit C approved subcontractors for independent consent obligations.

### pacwest-supply-agreement

This section addresses the Supply Agreement between Apex (as Supplier) and PacWest Water Authority (counterparty), governed by Texas law.

The contract contains a broad Change of Control definition at Section 1.1(c), which provides that "'Change of Control' shall mean (i) any merger, consolidation, or reorganization of Supplier with or into another entity, (ii) the sale or transfer of all or substantially all of the assets of Supplier, (iii) any transaction or series of related transactions resulting in any person or group of persons (as such terms are used in Section 13(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended) acquiring beneficial ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding voting securities of Supplier, or (iv) any direct or indirect change in the ultimate ownership or control of Supplier." The inclusion of limb (iv) means that even indirect changes of control — including those effected through a reverse-triangular merger in which Apex survives as a wholly-owned subsidiary — fall squarely within the definition.

The anti-assignment clause at Section 12.2 independently reinforces this exposure, providing that "Apex shall not assign this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of PacWest, which consent may be withheld in PacWest's sole discretion. Any attempted assignment in violation of this Section 12.2 shall be null and void and of no force or effect." The phrase "by operation of law or otherwise" captures reverse-triangular merger structures even where Apex remains the surviving legal entity. Section 12.2 further clarifies that a Change of Control is not deemed an assignment for purposes of that section but is instead governed exclusively by Section 10.5 — which applies the same absolute-discretion consent standard.

Section 10.5(b)(ii) grants PacWest a termination right upon Change of Control on 90 days' notice, with no cure period available to Apex. No termination fee or buyout formula was extracted. The minimum annual revenue exposure under this Agreement is $4,000,000 USD; no revenue concentration percentage, equity acceleration value, or single-trigger acceleration data was extracted. Dependent systems include NSF/ANSI 61, NSF/ANSI 372, ISO 9001:2015, SCADA-compatible interface modules, and AWWA standards, the continuity of which must be confirmed post-closing.

The risk rating for this contract is HIGH. PacWest holds an absolute-discretion consent and termination right with no cure period, the Change of Control definition expressly covers indirect changes of control and triggers regardless of merger structure, and the "operation of law" language in Section 12.2 creates a second independent trigger. The $4M revenue floor moderates — but does not eliminate — severity.

Action items: (1) Obtain PacWest's written consent under Section 10.5 prior to or promptly following closing, noting the 60-day post-closing window in Section 10.5(c). (2) Deliver written notice to PacWest within 10 business days of consummation per Section 10.5(a). (3) Negotiate elevation of the consent standard from sole discretion to not-unreasonably-withheld as a pre-closing condition. (4) Confirm the Texas UCC § 2-210 analysis for the "operation of law or otherwise" language in Section 12.2. (5) Assess trailing-twelve-month actual revenue above the $4M minimum to refine exposure. (6) Confirm post-closing maintenance of ISO 9001:2015, NSF/ANSI 61, and NSF/ANSI 372 compliance to avoid a Section 10.3 termination-for-cause trigger. (7) Confirm that the proposed merger structure does not constitute a "direct or indirect change in the ultimate ownership or control" under Section 1.1(c)(iv) prior to structuring disclosure.

### product-liability-policy

This section addresses the product liability insurance policy (Policy No. not separately identified; contract identifier: product-liability-policy) issued by Great Lakes Indemnity Company to the Named Insured, governed by the laws of Ohio.

The Policy contains an express Change of Control definition in Section II, which provides that "'Change of Control' means any of the following events: ... (b) any merger, consolidation, amalgamation, or statutory share exchange involving the Named Insured in which the Named Insured is not the surviving entity or in which the Named Insured survives but the holders of the Named Insured's voting securities immediately prior to such transaction hold less than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities of the surviving entity immediately after such transaction; ... (d) any transaction or series of related transactions that results in a change in the ultimate controlling person or entity of the Named Insured." Critically, this definition is broad enough to capture a reverse-triangular merger structure: even though the Named Insured survives as the legal entity post-merger, clauses (b) and (d) key on the ownership shift rather than on a direct assignment of the Policy. No separate change-of-control definition qualifying indirect transfers is provided (coc_includes_indirect: False), but the breadth of clause (d) achieves a functionally equivalent result.

Section IV.E contains the anti-assignment provision: "This Policy and any rights hereunder shall not be assigned or transferred by the Named Insured without the prior written consent of the Insurer, which consent may be withheld in the Insurer's sole and absolute discretion. Any purported assignment or transfer without such consent shall be void and of no effect." The clause does not include 'operation of law or otherwise' language, meaning that a reverse-triangular merger does not technically constitute an assignment — however, this offers no practical protection because Section IV.F.1 imposes an automatic run-off conversion upon any Change of Control event, with zero notice days and zero cure days, immediately upon closing. No termination fee amount or buyout formula has been extracted. Section IV.F.5 additionally bars any successor entity from coverage, eliminating prospective products liability coverage ($25M aggregate, $5M per-occurrence) for all post-closing products across a business generating approximately $187.4M in annual revenue. The Policy also cross-references Master Supply Agreement No. MSA-2019-0042 (Northland Refining Corporation) and Supply Agreement No. PWA-SUP-2021-117 (PacWest Water Authority) in connection with waiver of subrogation obligations, and operational continuity of the Crestline ERP Platform v.8.2 is material to claims administration under any run-off coverage.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL. The Change of Control definition in Section II is drafted to capture the proposed transaction regardless of merger structure, triggering immediate automatic run-off conversion under Section IV.F.1 with no notice and no cure period, creating an uninsured gap for post-closing product liability claims across $187.4M in annual revenue. The absolute-discretion consent standard under Section IV.E compounds the risk by foreclosing any reliable path to preserving prospective coverage by assignment.

Action Items: (1) Obtain outside insurance coverage counsel opinion confirming that the reverse-triangular merger triggers Section II(b) and (d) prior to signing the merger agreement. (2) Engage Great Lakes Indemnity Company immediately to negotiate a Change of Control endorsement or waiver preserving prospective coverage post-closing. (3) Pursue Insurer consent under Section IV.E prior to closing, identifying all available leverage. (4) Procure replacement products liability insurance for post-closing operations to eliminate the Section IV.F.5 coverage gap. (5) Evaluate purchasing the 36-month Extended Reporting Period Tail (Endorsement No. 1) at $853,125 for pre-closing product claims. (6) Deliver written Change of Control notice to the Insurer within 15 days of closing per Section IV.F.2. (7) Confirm Crestline ERP Platform v.8.2 continuity post-closing. (8) Verify that waiver of subrogation obligations under Endorsement No. 2 are replicated in replacement policies for the Northland Refining and PacWest Water Authority supply agreements. (9) Confirm that the Apex-Kenji Precision JV, LLC coverage limitations survive run-off and that the JV obtains independent coverage post-closing.

### hq-lease-crescent-ridge

This section addresses the HQ office lease (contract ID: hq-lease-crescent-ridge) between Tenant and counterparty Crescent Ridge Realty Partners, LP, governed by Ohio law.

The anti-assignment provision at Section 22.1 prohibits Tenant from assigning the Lease without prior written consent, stating that "[a]ny purported Transfer without Landlord's prior written consent shall be void and of no force or effect and shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 12.1(d)." Critically, Section 22.1 defines assignment to include "any assignment, transfer, or conveyance, whether voluntary or involuntary, by operation of law or otherwise," capturing involuntary transfers and operation-of-law conveyances.

Section 22.2 goes further by establishing a Deemed Assignment clause that expressly enumerates change-of-control events. It provides that any change in control of Tenant, "including without limitation any merger, consolidation, or transfer of a controlling interest in Tenant's equity, whether in a single transaction or a series of related transactions," constitutes a Deemed Assignment requiring Landlord's prior written consent. The definition of control under Section 22.2 encompasses indirect control "through the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise." Notably, Section 22.2 specifies that its provisions "shall apply regardless of the form of the transaction, including without limitation any transaction structured as a forward or reverse merger, triangular merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, recapitalization, or similar combination" — meaning a reverse-triangular merger by Acquirer is expressly and unambiguously named as a trigger. Indirect change-of-control is confirmed as in scope.

Consent is governed by Section 22.1 and Section 22.2, with a reasonableness standard, but Section 22.3 provides that Landlord silence within the response window is deemed a denial, not approval. Section 22.4(a) grants Landlord a hard termination right on 120 days' notice, with no cure period for unauthorized Deemed Assignments. Section 22.4(b) imposes an Early Termination Fee of $3,240,000, which must be reserved as a contingent liability. Annual rent exposure is $2,160,000. No revenue concentration percentage, equity acceleration value, or buyout formula was extracted. Cross-referenced instruments include Exhibit C (Work Letter) and a separate broker commission agreement with Meridian Commercial Realty Group, LLC, which should be reviewed independently.

Risk Rating: HIGH. The Deemed Assignment clause names reverse-triangular mergers explicitly, the termination right carries no cure period, the Early Termination Fee is $3,240,000, and $2,160,000 in annual rent is at risk if consent is withheld.

Action Items: (1) Obtain Crescent Ridge Realty Partners, LP's express prior written consent under Sections 22.1 and 22.2 before closing. (2) Submit the consent request with all required financial information at least 30 days before the proposed closing date to start the 20-business-day response clock under Section 22.3. (3) Do not close without express written consent in hand — Landlord silence is deemed a denial under Section 22.3. (4) Confirm acquirer's tangible net worth satisfies the Section 22.3(a) threshold. (5) Reserve $3,240,000 as a contingent liability in deal models. (6) Assess assignability of the Renewal Option under Section 3.3, which is personal to Tenant. (7) Verify no Event of Default exists at the time of the Transfer request and confirm the $360,000 Security Deposit under Section 5 is fully funded.
